content: The studies reviewed did not include any comparative analyses regarding the initiation timing of maternal antiretroviral therapy (ART) and breastfeeding practices. Specifically, the studies by Ngoma et al. (2015), Sagay et al. (2015), and Okafor et al. (2014) were cohort studies. The risk of bias was downgraded twice due to significant limitations in the studies. For instance, Sagay et al. (2015) lacked detailed feeding history, and Okafor et al. (2014) did not provide clear criteria for estimating HIV-free survival. Inconsistencies were noted, leading to a single downgrade. There was substantial heterogeneity in the pooled estimates, with an I-squared value of 82%. HIV-free survival rates varied significantly, ranging from 87% (95% CI: 79%-92%) in Ngoma et al. (2015) to 98% (95% CI: 97%-99%) in Sagay et al. (2015). Indirectness was also downgraded once because the research questions in the studies were not fully aligned with the PICO framework, and there were slight differences in co-interventions. For example, in Ngoma et al. (2015), all women were on ART. In Sagay et al. (2015) and Okafor et al. (2014), in addition to maternal ART, HIV-exposed infants received nevirapine (NVP) from birth up to six weeks. Two studies, Thomas et al. (2011) and Shapiro et al. (2013), were cohort studies embedded within randomized controlled trials. The risk of bias in Thomas et al. (2011) was downgraded once due to the lack of detailed feeding history, which posed a potential risk of selection bias. Inconsistencies were again noted, with a single downgrade due to substantial heterogeneity (I-squared = 97%). HIV-free survival rates ranged from 81%-87% (95% CI) in Thomas et al. (2010) to 92%-96% (95% CI) in Shapiro et al. (2013). Indirectness was downgraded once because the research questions were not fully aligned with the PICO framework. In Shapiro et al. (2013), women received different ART regimens based on their CD4 cell counts. In Thomas et al. (2011), all mothers were on ART, and all infants received a single dose of NVP within 72 hours of birth, followed by TMP/SMX from six weeks onward.
